System blueprint

A measurable customer retention workflow

Connect customer lifecycle evidence to relevant, approved actions. Define onboarding, value milestones, follow-up, and renewal signals so the team can investigate friction and improve customer experience with a clear owner.

Level 2Choose a capability

A decline in retention can reflect different customer groups, immature cohorts, unclear value, or a missed handoff. Teams need consistent lifecycle definitions and a way to connect evidence to suitable customer actions without treating an automated message as the solution.

Useful outputs

  • A customer lifecycle and cohort specification with agreed value milestones.
  • Eligible communication and owner-action workflows with clear stop conditions.
  • A retention and churn view with matched populations and observation windows.
  • An operating review guide and prioritized improvement backlog.

Inputs we need

  • Customer identity, lifecycle and value-event records, and eligible cohort definitions.
  • Approved communication preferences, customer feedback, content, and account ownership.
  • Observation windows, renewal context, provider access, and intervention criteria.
Level 3Explore a focus

Define the customer lifecycle

Agree customer identity, eligible populations, value milestones, and cohort windows. Connect approved commercial and product records and define the signals that need investigation.

Human expertise

Own the judgment.

Customer owners approve lifecycle actions, customer-facing content, and relationship decisions. Product and analysts validate value milestones, cohorts, calculation definitions, and the interpretation of changes.

AI assistance

Support the process.

AI can organize feedback, draft approved-context communication, and suggest investigation categories. People review sensitive or uncertain cases and decide how to address the customer need.
